sorry, I have no idea about it. 

/unassign

### The test(s) and what goes wrong

This issue report "...the same nodes" but also the similar test "...on different nodes" fails in the same way. The tests goes like this:

1. A UDP service is created with "type:LoadBalancer"
2. Wait until a loadBalancerIP is assigned
3. Start sending UDP packets to the service in 1s interval **with a fixed source-port**
4. Create _one_ endpoint POD
5. Wait until a reply is received, which should contain the POD hostname. **This is where it fails!**
6. Start a second endpoint POD on the same or a different node (the two test cases)
7. Delete the first endpoint POD
8. Verify that the second now receives the traffic by checking the "hostname" in the reply packets

_It should be noted that it is UDP traffic to the first endpoint POD that fails_

### Status so far

The focus has been on invalid conntrack entries, which has been fixed in a several PRs on both proxiers and recently been unified in common code in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116171.

UDP traffic may be sent:
1. Before the loadBalancerIP is configured on the node by `kube-proxy`
2. When the loadBalancerIP is configured on the node by `kube-proxy` but before any endpoint exist

Or at any point during on-going reconfiguration. A scenario is described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118844#issuecomment-1607964288, but this is fairly simple to [test manually](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118844#issuecomment-1608269856), and it seem to work.

@aroradaman has also found a possible correlation between failures and traffic entering on a node where the endpoint POD is **not** running. Test made with "externalTrafficPolicy:Local" which seem to fix the problem in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118938

Inspired by https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cloud-provider-kind by @aojea I realized that the only thing needed to run these tests on any local cluster (not necessarily KinD) is to allocate loadBalancerIP's and have a working route to those addresses. This can be done with `metallb` or, as in my case, a simple loadBalancerIP allocator and a static route. I have 4 K8s nodes and a static route to one of them, so there should be a 1/4 probability that traffic enters a local node (in theory).

I can now run both tests in ~8s and can use `--repeat` to `ginkgo`. I have executed the 2 tests 100 times without any error. This does not mean that there is no fault in K8s, but that the problem only occurs on GCE. It can be a problem in the environment, or for instance that the timing in GCE clusters exposes a K8s bug.
